title: Adding and subtracting coplanar vectors enrichment

evidence.role: Direct retrieval is grounded in the independently verified Lesson 9 handoff and controlled vector definition.

hints: Recall the property that a scalar does not require.
A complete numerical report needs more than a bare number.

walkthrough.text: Retrieve the exact Lesson 9 definition: a vector quantity is a physical quantity that has magnitude and direction.
Translate magnitude into a numerical report by including its numerical size and appropriate unit.
Add the direction because it is required to specify the vector completely.

ai_rubric.observable: States that a vector quantity is a physical quantity that has magnitude and direction
States that a complete numerical vector report includes magnitude, an appropriate unit and direction

evidence.role: Grounds correct vector placement and the direction of a resultant arrow in original wording.

hints: The second move begins where the first move ends.
The resultant must connect the original start to the final point.

walkthrough.text: Place A first and preserve its magnitude and direction.
Move B parallel to itself until its tail meets A's head.
Draw the resultant from A's tail to B's head, which matches option A.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects A as the correct head-to-tail construction for vector addition

evidence.role: Directly grounds opposite-collinear resultant demand while the values and context remain original.

hints: Opposite directions cause partial cancellation.
The final direction follows the larger vector.

walkthrough.text: The forces are collinear and opposite, so subtract their magnitudes.
Calculate 14 minus 9 to obtain a magnitude of 5 N.
The 14 N force is larger and points east, so the resultant is 5 N east and option B is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects B, giving a resultant of 5 N east

evidence.role: The retained evidence grounds vector construction and directional cancellation; explicit vector subtraction is a syllabus-owned evidence gap filled by the controlled lesson outcome.

hints: Rewrite subtraction as addition of an opposite vector.
Only the vector being subtracted changes direction.

walkthrough.text: Rewrite A minus B as A plus minus B.
Create minus B by reversing B while keeping its magnitude unchanged.
Add the reversed B to A head-to-tail, which is the operation described by option B.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects B, reversing vector B and adding the reversed vector to A head-to-tail

evidence.role: Grounds a head-to-tail route diagram and a perpendicular resultant calculation without any component resolution.

hints: Start the northward arrow where the eastward arrow ends.
The completed route is a right-angled triangle.

walkthrough.text: Draw 12 squares east and then 5 squares north from the first arrow's head.
Join the original start to the final point with R.
Use the right triangle to calculate the resultant magnitude and its angle measured north of east.

evidence.role: Grounds original head-to-tail construction and resultant-arrow direction.

hints: Use the stated grid scale for both vector lengths.
R begins at the route's start and ends at its finish.

walkthrough.text: From the start, draw 12 squares east with an arrowhead.
From that arrow's head, draw 5 squares north with an arrowhead.
Draw R from the original start to the final head and point its arrow toward the final point.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws the 12 km east and 5.0 km north vectors to scale in a correct head-to-tail chain
Draws and labels R from the original start to the final point with the correct arrow direction

evidence.role: Grounds use of Pythagoras on two already perpendicular vectors.

hints: The resultant is the hypotenuse, not the sum of the two side lengths.
Square the two perpendicular vector magnitudes before adding.

walkthrough.text: Read the perpendicular sides as 12 km and 5.0 km.
Calculate $R=\sqrt{12^2+5.0^2}=\sqrt{169}$.
Therefore the magnitude is 13 km, which lies between the longest side 12 km and the path sum 17 km.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the right-angled vector triangle to obtain a resultant magnitude of 13 km

evidence.role: Extends the retained vector-triangle construction to a direction calculation using school trigonometry.

hints: For an angle from east, identify the northward side as opposite.
Finish the numerical angle with its compass description.

walkthrough.text: Let theta be the angle between R and east.
Round to $22.6^\circ$ and state north of east because R points above the east direction.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses $\tan\theta=5.0/12$ for an angle measured north of east
Obtains a direction of $22.6^\circ$ north of east

evidence.role: Combines retained construction, cancellation and perpendicular-resultant demands into an original subtraction task.

hints: Change the subtraction into addition before drawing.
Use the resulting right triangle for magnitude and direction.

walkthrough.text: Reverse B so that its 3.0 m magnitude is directed south.
Add A and minus B head-to-tail and draw the southeast resultant.
Use the completed right triangle to calculate both magnitude and direction.

evidence.role: Grounds the construction and resultant direction; reversal is supplied by the syllabus subtraction outcome.

hints: Only B changes direction when it becomes minus B.
Place the reversed arrow at A's head.

walkthrough.text: Reverse the 3.0 m north arrow to make a 3.0 m south arrow.
Place the south arrow's tail at the head of the 7.0 m east arrow.
Draw R from the original origin to the final point, pointing south of east.

ai_rubric.observable: Reverses B to a 3.0 m south vector and places it head-to-tail after A
Draws and labels R from the original tail of A to the final head, directed south of east

evidence.role: Grounds calculation of a resultant from two already perpendicular vectors.

hints: Reversal changes direction but not the 3.0 m magnitude.
The two sides of the completed triangle remain perpendicular.

walkthrough.text: Use perpendicular side lengths 7.0 m and 3.0 m.
Round to 7.62 m. This is longer than 7.0 m and shorter than 10.0 m, as required.

ai_rubric.observable: Forms $R=\sqrt{7.0^2+3.0^2}$ from the completed right-angled vector triangle
Obtains a resultant magnitude of 7.62 m

evidence.role: Extends the retained vector triangle to a direction calculation without resolving an arbitrary vector.

hints: The requested angle starts from east.
Use the reversed vector's direction when naming the quadrant.

walkthrough.text: For the angle from east, use opposite 3.0 m and adjacent 7.0 m.
Round to $23.2^\circ$ and state south of east because B was reversed southward.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses $\tan\theta=3.0/7.0$ for an angle measured from east
Obtains a direction of $23.2^\circ$ south of east

evidence.role: Uses every retained mapped leaf to combine prior scalar-vector distinction, a multi-vector diagram, opposite-collinear cancellation and a perpendicular resultant.

hints: Separate the scalar time from the directed movements before drawing.
Combine the east-west pair before completing the final right triangle.

walkthrough.text: Use Lesson 9 definitions to classify time as scalar and all three displacements as vectors.
Draw the three movements head-to-tail and join the start to the finish.
Reduce the opposite horizontal movements, then calculate magnitude and direction from the remaining perpendicular pair.

evidence.role: Directly applies the verified Lesson 9 handoff inside a current-lesson route problem.

hints: Ask whether direction is part of each quantity's complete specification.
The time value describes duration rather than movement direction.

walkthrough.text: Time is a scalar quantity because it has magnitude only.
Each displacement is a vector because its complete statement includes a magnitude and a compass direction.
This distinction explains why 48 s is not drawn as an arrow while all three displacements are.

ai_rubric.observable: Classifies time as a scalar quantity because it has magnitude only
Classifies all three displacements as vector quantities because each has magnitude and direction

evidence.role: Grounds head-to-tail route construction and an arrow for the resultant direction.

hints: Begin each new movement at the previous arrow's head.
R connects the route's first tail to its final head.

walkthrough.text: From the start, draw 9 squares west and then 12 squares south.
From the second arrow's head, draw 4 squares east.
Draw and label R from the original start to the final point. It points southwest.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws the 9.0 m west, 12 m south and 4.0 m east vectors to scale in one continuous head-to-tail chain
Draws and labels R from the original start to the final point with the correct southwest direction

evidence.role: Grounds opposite-collinear cancellation followed by a perpendicular resultant calculation.

hints: The westward and eastward movements partly cancel.
After that cancellation, the remaining directions are perpendicular.

walkthrough.text: Combine the horizontal movements: 9.0 m west minus 4.0 m east gives 5.0 m west. The southward movement remains 12 m.
Calculate $R=\sqrt{5.0^2+12^2}=\sqrt{169}=13$ m.
For an angle from west, calculate $\theta=\tan^{-1}(12/5.0)=67.380...^\circ$.
State $67.4^\circ$ south of west. The southwest direction agrees with the drawn route, and 13 m exceeds the longer 12 m side but is below 17 m.

ai_rubric.observable: Combines the opposing horizontal displacements to obtain 5.0 m west while retaining 12 m south
Forms $R=\sqrt{5.0^2+12^2}$ from the final right-angled vector triangle
Obtains a resultant magnitude of 13 m
Obtains a direction of $67.4^\circ$ south of west or an equivalent unambiguous direction

later_learning_excluded: resolving a vector into perpendicular components
component equations for arbitrary vector systems
later-topic force, motion or field laws

quality_audit.originality: All learner wording, numerical values, route contexts and planned figure briefs are original. No official diagram or wording is reproduced.
quality_audit.scope: The package teaches only addition and subtraction of complete coplanar vectors through head-to-tail geometry, collinear cancellation, perpendicular triangles and scale drawings.
quality_audit.evidence: All four retained Lesson 10 P2 leaves and their complete source-question contexts were reviewed. Removed component-resolution leaves were excluded. P1 evidence is deferred and was not inferred.
quality_audit.numerical_recomputation: All lesson values were independently recomputed: 10.0 km at 53.13010235 degrees, 9.848857802 m at 23.96248897 degrees, the 5 N collinear subtraction, 13 km at 22.61986495 degrees, 7.615773106 m at 23.19859051 degrees, and 13 m at 67.38013505 degrees, with the stated rounded values and directional checks confirmed.
quality_audit.dependency_audit: Exactly two learner-visible questions exercise dependency: q01 directly retrieves the Lesson 9 vector definition and reporting contract, while q07 mixes that distinction with current vector addition.
later_knowledge_excluded: sine and cosine component selection for an arbitrary vector
later-topic physical principles from mixed paper contexts
